content_html:
Tragic Loss of Beloved Hippo Fiona

The Cincinnati Zoo in Ohio has announced the devastating death of its world-famous hippopotamus, Fiona, just days after she swallowed a knitted hat that accidentally slipped into her enclosure. Zoo officials stated that Fiona fought until she could not fight anymore, despite intensive medical intervention from veterinary and keeper teams who tried everything possible to save her.

The incident occurred roughly 10 days before her death when a visitor tossed a hat into the air, which was caught by a ceiling fan and flung through a small opening into the habitat. Although Fiona initially appeared fine, her appetite declined a few days later as veterinary staff monitored her condition and attempted to help her pass the obstruction naturally.

Medical Efforts and Emergency Interventions

  • Vets utilized an ultrasound showing the hat passing into Fiona's small intestine, while ruling out surgery as unviable for full-grown hippos.
  • The animal care team borrowed a vibration plate platform from a local horse farm to encourage the foreign object to pass.
  • Zoo director Dave Jenike and spokesperson Michelle Curley confirmed that staff exhausted all possible heroic measures before her passing.

Global Legacy of an Internet Icon

Fiona first rose to international prominence after her premature birth at the Cincinnati Zoo in 2017. Weighing a mere 13 kg (29 lbs)—roughly half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species—she immediately captured public affection by fighting against the odds to survive and grow into a healthy animal.

Over the years, her resilience made her a beloved social media star and a symbol of hope for millions of fans worldwide. Following her sudden passing, local leaders including Cincinnati's mayor reflected on the profound joy she brought to countless lives throughout her remarkable life at the zoo.
